The story starts with Adam. What does it mean that all people share one beginning?
Abraham's line continues through Isaac and Israel. How does God keep his promises through families?
The sons of Israel are named one by one. What does it show that God knows each family?
Even failures are recorded honestly in Judah's line. How does God work through imperfect families?
David's family is listed. How does God's promise to David shape this record?
The royal line continues even after exile. What does this show about God's faithfulness?
Jabez prayed, "Oh that you would bless me... and that your hand might be with me." What would you ask God?
"And God granted what he asked." How does this encourage your prayers?
They cried out to God in battle and he answered because they trusted him. How does trust shape prayer?
The tribes were unfaithful and went into exile. What does this teach about the cost of turning away?
David put men in charge of song in the house of the Lord. How does music help you worship?
The priests made atonement as God commanded. How does Jesus fulfil the priestly work?
The families are counted as mighty warriors. What does this record show about God's people?
Ephraim mourned for his sons, and God gave him another. How does God bring comfort after loss?
Benjamin's family is listed in detail. What does it mean that God remembers every name?
Saul's descendants are recorded. How does God's story include even those who failed?
Israel was taken into exile because of unfaithfulness. What does returning to God look like?
Gatekeepers kept watch faithfully every morning. How can you serve faithfully in small, regular ways?
The singers were on duty day and night. How can your life be filled with praise?
Saul's life ended in defeat. What does his story teach?
Saul died because he did not seek guidance from the Lord. How do you seek God's guidance?
All Israel came to David as God had promised. How does God fulfil his word?
David became greater, for the Lord of hosts was with him. What does God's presence make possible?
David's mighty men risked their lives for a drink of water for him. What does loyal love look like?
Amasai said, "Peace be to you, for your God helps you." How can you bless others?
The men of Issachar understood the times and knew what Israel ought to do. How can you understand your times wisely?
There was joy in Israel as they made David king. What brings joy to God's people?
David consulted his leaders and sought God's will together. How can decisions be made together before God?
Uzzah died when he touched the ark. What does this teach about God's holiness?
David inquired of God before battle. How often do you ask God first?
The fame of David went out into all lands. How does God make his name known through his people?
David prepared a place for the ark. How can you prepare your heart for God?
This time they carried the ark as God commanded. Why does doing things God's way matter?
They brought up the ark with shouting and music. How do you celebrate God's presence?
"Give thanks to the Lord; call upon his name; make known his deeds." Which of these can you do today?
"Declare his glory among the nations." How can you declare God's glory?
"Oh give thanks to the Lord, for he is good; for his steadfast love endures forever!" What are you thankful for?
God told David that he had not asked for a house of cedar. How do you respond when God redirects your plans?
God promised a son whose throne would be established forever. How does this point to Jesus?
David prayed, "Who am I, O Lord God?" How does God's grace humble you?
"The Lord gave victory to David wherever he went." How has God helped you?
David administered justice and equity to all his people. How can you act justly?
David's kindness was rejected and his servants were humiliated. How do you respond when kindness is rejected?
"Be strong, and let us use our strength for our people... and may the Lord do what seems good to him." What can you entrust to God?
David stayed in Jerusalem while the army went out. What does the story in 2 Samuel tell us happened then?
Giants were defeated by David's servants. How does God work through ordinary people?
David sinned by numbering the people. What do you trust in instead of God?
David said, "Let me fall into the hand of the Lord, for his mercy is very great." How does this show trust?
David would not offer God what cost him nothing. What does costly worship look like?
David prepared materials for the temple Solomon would build. How can you prepare the way for others?
"Be strong and courageous. Fear not; do not be dismayed." Where do you need courage?
David said, "Set your mind and heart to seek the Lord." How can you do this today?
David organised the Levites for service. How does order help worship?
The Levites stood every morning and evening to thank and praise the Lord. How can you begin and end your day with praise?
The priests were divided fairly by lot. How does fairness matter in God's work?
The heads of families and the youngest served alike. What does this show about everyone having a place?
Musicians prophesied with lyres, harps and cymbals in thanksgiving and praise. How does music help you praise God?
Small and great, teacher and pupil, all took their turn. How can different people serve together?
Gatekeepers guarded the house of the Lord. How can you guard what is holy in your life?
Treasurers looked after the gifts dedicated to the Lord. How can you be faithful with what is God's?
The army was organised month by month. How does God use organisation in his work?
David's counsellors were wise men. Who are your wise counsellors?
David told the leaders to seek all the commandments of the Lord. How can you seek God's ways?
"Know the God of your father and serve him with a whole heart and a willing mind." What does this look like for you?
"Be strong and courageous... for the Lord God, even my God, is with you." What task do you need God's help with?
The leaders gave willingly and the people rejoiced. What brings joy in giving?
David prayed, "Yours, O Lord, is the greatness and the power and the glory." What can you praise God for?
David asked, "Who am I... that we should be able to offer willingly? For all things come from you." How does this shape your giving?
